definitions.explanation: A collective revolt or armed uprising, historically referring to peasant rebellions in feudal Japan. The participants banded together to resist oppressive taxes, famine conditions, or unjust rule.

examples.japanese: {農民|のうみん}が{一揆|いっき}を{起|お}こした。
{重|おも}い{年貢|ねんぐ}に{耐|た}えかねて、{一揆|いっき}が{各地|かくち}で{起|お}きた。
examples.english: Unable to bear the heavy taxes, uprisings broke out in various regions.

examples.japanese: {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}には{百姓|ひゃくしょう}{一揆|いっき}が{数多|かずおお}く{記録|きろく}されている。
examples.english: Numerous peasant uprisings are recorded from the Edo period.

notes:
USAGE: {一揆|いっき} primarily appears in historical contexts. It refers specifically to collective uprisings in pre-modern Japan, particularly during the {室町|むろまち}{時代|じだい} and {江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一揆|いっき}を{起|お}こす (to stage an uprising)
- {百姓|ひゃくしょう}{一揆|いっき} (peasant uprising)
- {一向|いっこう}{一揆|いっき} (Ikkō-ikki, religious uprisings by Pure Land Buddhists)
- {土|つち}{一揆|いっき} (land uprising, riots demanding debt cancellation)

ETYMOLOGY: {一|いっ} (one, united) + {揆|き} (action, measure). The word originally meant "acting as one" or "of one mind," emphasizing the collective nature of the movement.

NOTE: Do not confuse with {一気|いっき} (in one breath, all at once), which is a different word.
